title: Milestone 4 quarto website
text:
This is a Quarto website created for a simple course project.

Visit my local Quarto website



Quarto lets you combine narrative text, code, and visualizations in a webpage.



The example below uses a real public dataset from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) API for the last five years and visualizes the monthly pattern in the U.S. unemployment rate.

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

fred_url <- "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE"

unrate <- readr::read_csv(fred_url, show_col_types = FALSE)

colnames(unrate) <- c("date", "unemployment_rate")

unrate <- unrate |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2021-09-01")) |>
  arrange(date)

ggplot(unrate, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c7fb8", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "#d95f0e", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Unemployment Rate, Last Five Years",
    subtitle = "Monthly FRED UNRATE data",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Unemployment rate (%)",
    caption = "Source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
